explain: Bedrock provides serverless API access to foundation models without provisioning infrastructure. The other options require manual hosting, training, or use an unrelated service.
options: Use Amazon Bedrock to access foundation models via a serverless API
Train a custom CNN classifier from scratch using SageMaker training
Launch GPU EC2 instances and manually install open-source LLM software
Use Amazon Rekognition to host a large language model for chat replies
q: A company wants to use a foundation model through an API without provisioning servers. Which service should it use?

explain: Comprehend performs NLP tasks such as sentiment analysis on unstructured text. Rekognition, Textract, and Transcribe handle images, documents, and speech instead.
options: Use Amazon Rekognition to detect sentiment labels inside product photos
Use Amazon Comprehend to detect sentiment in customer product reviews
Use Amazon Textract to extract sentiment scores from scanned invoices
Use Amazon Transcribe to translate sentiment from audio into subtitles
q: A retailer wants to detect positive or negative sentiment in thousands of written product reviews. Which service fits?

explain: Rekognition analyzes images and videos to detect objects, faces, and unsafe content. The other services process documents, speech, or text rather than photos.
options: Use Amazon Textract to detect faces and objects inside security camera photos
Use Amazon Comprehend to recognize celebrities and objects in stored images
Use Amazon Rekognition to detect objects and faces in uploaded user photos
Use Amazon Transcribe to convert image labels into searchable audio notes
q: A social app must detect objects, faces, and unsafe content in user-uploaded photos. Which service should it use?

explain: Textract extracts text, forms, and tables from scanned documents and PDFs. Rekognition identifies image content, Transcribe handles audio, and Polly synthesizes speech.
options: Use Amazon Rekognition celebrity detection to digitize printed loan forms
Use Amazon Transcribe streaming to extract tables from scanned PDF pages
Use Amazon Polly neural voices to read printed mortgage forms into text
Use Amazon Textract to extract text and tables from scanned loan forms
q: A bank must digitize scanned loan applications, including text, forms, and tables. Which service should it use?

explain: Transcribe converts speech to text, including batch and streaming audio. Polly does the reverse, while Comprehend and Rekognition process text and images.
options: Use Amazon Transcribe to convert recorded support calls into text logs
Use Amazon Polly to transcribe recorded agent calls into written notes
Use Amazon Comprehend to decode audio waveforms directly into transcripts
Use Amazon Rekognition to transcribe spoken dialogue from video soundtracks
q: A call center wants to convert recorded customer support calls into searchable text. Which service should it use?

explain: Personalize builds personalized product and content recommendations from user behavior. Forecast predicts time series, while Bedrock and Lex serve different purposes.
options: Use Amazon Forecast to recommend products from each shopper browsing history
Use Amazon Personalize to recommend products based on shopper behavior
Use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to generate recommendations from purchase logs
Use Amazon Lex intents and slots to rank personalized product suggestions
q: An online store wants personalized product recommendations based on each shopper's browsing and purchase history. Which service fits?

explain: Forecast is the time-series forecasting service for demand, inventory, and capacity planning. Personalize recommends items and Comprehend analyzes text instead.
options: Use Amazon Personalize predictors to forecast next-quarter sales quantities
Use Amazon Comprehend topic modeling to project future inventory demand levels
Use Amazon Forecast to predict future product demand from history
Use Amazon Textract table extraction to estimate seasonal sales forecasts
q: A retailer wants to predict next-quarter product demand from historical sales data. Which service should it use?

explain: Polly converts text into lifelike speech for announcements and voice apps. Transcribe does the reverse, while Forecast and Textract handle numbers and documents.
options: Use Amazon Transcribe batch jobs to speak flight updates over loudspeakers
Use Amazon Forecast predictors to generate spoken gate announcements
Use Amazon Textract OCR output to vocalize departure boards in terminals
Use Amazon Polly to convert flight status text into spoken announcements
q: An airport wants to turn written flight-status updates into natural-sounding spoken announcements. Which service should it use?

explain: Lex builds conversational chatbots with intents, slots, and dialog management. Polly only synthesizes speech, while Connect routing and Bedrock agents differ in scope.
options: Use Amazon Lex to build a chatbot that books appointments with intents
Use Amazon Polly neural voices to manage booking dialogues and user slots
Use Amazon Connect contact flows alone to parse free-text booking requests
Use Amazon Transcribe medical mode to run the appointment booking dialogue
q: A clinic wants a website chatbot that books appointments by understanding patient requests. Which service should it use?

explain: Knowledge Bases connect Bedrock models to company documents for RAG-grounded answers. Fine-tuning retrains weights, while Guardrails filter content rather than retrieve it.
options: Fine-tune a Bedrock model on manuals so document retrieval becomes unneeded
Use Bedrock Knowledge Bases to ground answers in company policy documents
Apply Bedrock Guardrails filters to retrieve relevant manual passages for RAG
Export the manuals to SageMaker training jobs for nightly batch inference
q: A company wants its Bedrock assistant to answer using internal policy documents without retraining the model. What should it use?

explain: Guardrails enforce denied topics, content filters, and PII redaction on model inputs and outputs. Knowledge Bases retrieve documents and Agents call tools instead.
options: Use Bedrock Agents action groups to block disallowed advice in responses
Use Bedrock Knowledge Bases chunking to filter out harmful model replies
Use Bedrock Guardrails to block disallowed topics and redact PII data
Use Bedrock provisioned throughput to throttle and filter sensitive replies
q: A firm must block disallowed advice topics and redact personal data in chatbot replies. Which Bedrock feature should it use?

explain: Bedrock Agents decompose tasks, reason, and call tools such as Lambda functions and APIs. A plain model invocation cannot act, while Guardrails only filter content.
options: Use a single Bedrock InvokeModel call with a longer prompt to book tickets
Use Bedrock Guardrails content filters to execute booking API calls directly
Use a Bedrock Knowledge Base sync job to place orders through backend APIs
Use Bedrock Agents to reason over the request and call booking APIs
q: A travel site wants an assistant that checks availability and books trips by calling backend APIs. Which Bedrock feature fits?

explain: JumpStart provides prebuilt foundation models deployable into SageMaker with a few clicks. Training from scratch or hosting on EC2 manually adds unneeded effort.
options: Use SageMaker JumpStart to deploy a prebuilt foundation model endpoint
Train a transformer from random weights on EC2 Spot with custom scripts
Use Amazon Rekognition labels to deploy a text generation model endpoint
Export Bedrock Guardrails rules into a SageMaker hosting configuration
q: A team wants to deploy a prebuilt foundation model into SageMaker quickly without training from scratch. What should it use?

explain: Bedrock does not use customer inputs or prompts to train its base models. Data stays within the service and is not shared with other customers or model providers.
options: Bedrock adds customer prompts to public training sets to improve base models
Bedrock does not train base models on customer prompts or private data
Bedrock shares encrypted customer data with providers for model retraining
Bedrock publishes customer Knowledge Base content for benchmark datasets
q: A security team asks whether Amazon Bedrock trains shared models on their prompts and documents. What is the correct answer?

explain: On-demand Bedrock inference bills per input and output token processed. There is no hourly endpoint charge, unlike provisioned throughput or SageMaker endpoints.
options: Bedrock on-demand bills a flat monthly fee per model regardless of usage
Bedrock on-demand bills per provisioned model unit reserved each month
Bedrock on-demand bills per input and output token actually processed
Bedrock on-demand bills per training image indexed in Knowledge Bases
q: How is Amazon Bedrock priced when a team uses on-demand inference with no throughput commitment?

explain: RAG retrieves current documents at query time, so fast-changing catalogs stay fresh without retraining. Fine-tuning suits stable style or domain knowledge instead.
options: Fine-tune the model nightly on catalog dumps to memorize prices and stock
Use Bedrock provisioned throughput so the model memorizes product details
Train a SageMaker classifier that rewrites catalog facts into model weights
Use RAG with a Knowledge Base so answers cite current catalog documents
q: A support chatbot must answer from a product catalog that changes daily. Should the team choose RAG or fine-tuning, and why?

explain: Fine-tuning teaches stable domain vocabulary, tone, and formats that RAG retrieval alone cannot enforce. Frequently changing facts still belong in a Knowledge Base.
options: Fine-tune the model so it learns stable legal vocabulary, tone, and format
Rebuild the Knowledge Base hourly so the model adopts the formal writing tone
Raise the sampling temperature so outputs randomly match the legal style
Add Guardrails denied-topic lists to teach the model formal legal phrasing
q: A law firm wants contract summaries always written in a specific formal style with domain vocabulary. Which approach fits best?

explain: Knowledge Bases split documents into chunks, embed them, and retrieve the most relevant passages at query time. The foundation model weights remain unchanged.
options: Knowledge Bases retrain model weights nightly on newly uploaded documents
Knowledge Bases chunk and embed documents, retrieving passages at query time
Knowledge Bases convert PDFs into Guardrails rules that rewrite user prompts
Knowledge Bases duplicate each document into model context for every request
q: How does an Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base make company documents available to a foundation model?

explain: Agents use action groups backed by Lambda functions or APIs, with schemas describing available operations. Guardrails filter content and Knowledge Bases supply documents.
options: Agents store API credentials inside the prompt text for each user request
Agents rely on Guardrails thresholds to decide which Lambda to execute
Agents call Lambda-backed action groups defined by API schemas they use
Agents query Knowledge Base embeddings to run database write operations
q: A Bedrock Agent must look up orders and issue refunds by calling internal APIs. How does the agent execute these actions?

explain: Guardrails support denied topics, sensitive-information filters with PII redaction, and word filters. They do not retrain models or manage network access.
options: Configure provisioned throughput quotas to redact names in model responses
Define Knowledge Base chunk sizes that automatically mask account numbers
Write agent Lambda code that fine-tunes the model away from advice topics
Configure Guardrails denied topics plus PII filters to block and redact
q: A bank chatbot must refuse investment advice and mask account numbers in replies. How should the team implement this?

explain: Automatic evaluation uses metrics on labeled datasets for speed, while human evaluation judges quality and safety nuances. Guardrails enforce policy but do not score accuracy.
options: Use automatic metrics for quick scoring plus human review for quality nuance
Use Guardrails thresholds as the accuracy score for each candidate model
Use provisioned throughput levels to rank which model answers most safely
Use Knowledge Base sync frequency as the main measure of model quality
q: A team must compare two Bedrock models on summarization quality and safety before launch. Which evaluation approach is sound?

explain: Provisioned throughput reserves model capacity for steady high-volume workloads needing consistent latency. Sporadic workloads are cheaper on pay-per-token on-demand pricing.
options: Use on-demand inference for steady traffic because reservations lower costs
Use provisioned throughput for steady high-volume traffic needing stable latency
Use model evaluation jobs to reserve capacity for production inference traffic
Use Knowledge Base storage quotas to guarantee model inference throughput
q: An app sends steady high-volume Bedrock traffic and needs consistent latency with committed usage. Which option fits?

explain: Transcribe supports real-time streaming transcription for live captioning. Comprehend analyzes text afterward, while Polly and Textract serve other modalities.
options: Use Amazon Polly streaming synthesis to caption live broadcasts in real time
Use Amazon Comprehend streaming entities to transcribe live speech to text
Use Amazon Transcribe streaming to generate live captions from speech audio
Use Amazon Textract streaming OCR to transcribe spoken webinar dialogue
q: A media company needs real-time captions generated from live broadcast speech. Which service and mode should it use?

explain: AnalyzeDocument extracts forms, tables, and key-value pairs, while DetectDocumentText only reads raw text. Comprehend analyzes language rather than document layout.
options: Use Textract DetectDocumentText to extract key-value pairs from tax forms
Use Comprehend syntax analysis to reconstruct tables from scanned pages
Use Rekognition text detection to parse key-value pairs from claim forms
Use Textract AnalyzeDocument to extract forms, tables, and key-value pairs
q: An insurer must extract key-value pairs and tables from scanned claim forms, not just raw text lines. Which operation fits?

explain: Rekognition Video handles stored and streaming video for labels, faces, and unsafe content. Image-only APIs cannot process video timelines or streams.
options: Use Rekognition Video to detect labels and unsafe scenes in archived footage
Use Rekognition still-image calls frame by frame for live stream moderation
Use Comprehend video mode to label objects across recorded video streams
Use Textract video OCR to flag unsafe activities in surveillance footage
q: A platform must detect labels, faces, and unsafe scenes across hours of archived video. Which Rekognition capability fits?

explain: Comprehend custom classification and entity recognition train on company-labeled examples for domain-specific categories and entities. Generic built-in APIs lack that customization.
options: Use Comprehend built-in sentiment to classify tickets into company categories
Use Comprehend custom classification trained on labeled company tickets
Use Transcribe custom language models to categorize written support tickets
Use Rekognition custom labels to extract entities from plain text tickets
q: A firm needs support tickets classified into its own custom categories using labeled historical tickets. Which approach fits?

explain: Real-time PutEvents updates user behavior so recommendations reflect the current session. Retraining from scratch per click is slow and unnecessary.
options: Retrain the Personalize solution after every click to refresh recommendations
Rebuild the entire interactions dataset nightly and ignore live click events
Send PutEvents in real time so recommendations reflect the current session
Switch the campaign to Forecast predictors for session-aware recommendations
q: A video service wants recommendations to adapt within the current viewing session as users click. How should it feed the signal?

explain: What-if analysis simulates how promos or price changes would affect the forecast without altering history. Accuracy metrics and backtesting measure quality instead.
options: Run backtesting exports to simulate the effect of a planned price increase
Retrain the predictor on invented future rows to preview promotion effects
Change historical sales figures directly to model the upcoming promotion
Use Forecast what-if analysis to simulate the promotion impact on demand
q: A planner wants to preview how a planned promotion would change the demand forecast without editing history. Which feature fits?

explain: Lex intents with slots and dialog management collect structured details like dates and destinations. Plain FAQ retrieval cannot run multi-turn slot filling.
options: Use Lex intents with slots to collect destination, dates, and passengers
Use Polly lexicon files to parse travel dates from free-text user input
Use Transcribe vocabulary filters to manage multi-turn booking dialogues
Use Comprehend sentiment scores to fill booking slots from user replies
q: A Lex travel bot must collect destination, dates, and passenger count across multiple turns. Which Lex modeling approach fits?

explain: Polly neural and long-form voices produce natural narration for books and articles. Transcribe converts speech to text, which is the opposite direction.
options: Use Amazon Transcribe dictation mode to narrate e-books from written text
Use Amazon Polly neural voices to narrate e-books from written chapters
Use Amazon Comprehend reading mode to vocalize long-form book chapters
Use Amazon Rekognition narration to speak book text from cover images
q: A publisher wants written e-book chapters converted into natural long-form narration. Which service and voice type fit?

explain: Bedrock hosts third-party models such as Claude and Llama alongside Amazon Titan behind one API. SageMaker endpoints and direct provider contracts add unneeded complexity.
options: Sign separate hosting contracts with each provider and build custom gateways
Deploy each provider model on EC2 GPUs behind a hand-built routing layer
Use Bedrock to access Titan, Claude, and Llama models through one API
Use Rekognition model hosting to serve each text model on its own endpoint
q: A team wants to compare Titan, Claude, and Llama models through a single managed API. How should it access them?

explain: Private VPC endpoints plus KMS-managed keys keep Bedrock traffic and stored data under customer control. Public endpoints and provider-side logging weaken isolation.
options: Send Bedrock prompts over public internet and store logs in shared buckets
Allow all IAM principals full Bedrock access without VPC or key controls
Disable encryption so auditors can read Bedrock payloads more conveniently
Use VPC endpoints for Bedrock traffic and KMS keys for data encryption
q: A regulated firm must isolate Bedrock traffic from the public internet and control encryption keys. What should it configure?

explain: Lower temperature and top-p make output more deterministic and focused, while higher values increase randomness. Max tokens limits length rather than creativity.
options: Lower temperature and top-p to make Bedrock answers more deterministic
Raise temperature to maximum to force consistent and repeatable answers
Increase max tokens so the model becomes more factual and less random
Disable stop sequences so outputs converge on the single correct answer
q: Bedrock summary outputs vary too much between runs and the team wants consistent, focused answers. Which parameter change helps?

explain: RAG grounds answers in retrieved passages that can be cited and checked, reducing hallucinations. Longer prompts and higher temperature do not verify facts.
options: Increase the sampling temperature so the model invents fewer novel facts
Ground answers with RAG retrieval so outputs cite verifiable source passages
Lengthen the system prompt so the model memorizes more factual content
Switch to provisioned throughput so the same model hallucinates less often
q: A Bedrock assistant sometimes invents facts when answering from company documents. Which technique best reduces this?

explain: JumpStart supports selecting a foundation model, optionally fine-tuning it, and deploying to a SageMaker endpoint. Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Rekognition do not deploy SageMaker models.
options: Build a Bedrock Knowledge Base sync that provisions SageMaker endpoints
Train Rekognition Custom Labels and export the weights to an LLM endpoint
Use JumpStart to fine-tune a foundation model and deploy it on SageMaker
Configure Lex fulfillment webhooks to host the foundation model endpoint
q: A team wants to fine-tune an open foundation model and host it on its own SageMaker endpoint. Which JumpStart workflow fits?

explain: Guardrails apply to the final agent output, so tool results and drafted replies are filtered before the user sees them. Filtering only inputs or tools leaves the final text unchecked.
options: Apply Guardrails only to the user input and trust the agent final answer
Filter each Lambda tool result and skip checking the final agent reply
Replace Guardrails with Knowledge Base ranking to enforce safety policy
Apply Guardrails to the final agent output including tool-derived content
q: A Bedrock Agent calls pricing APIs and drafts replies that must never include disallowed content. Where should Guardrails apply?

explain: Provisioned throughput pays a time-based commitment, which wins for sustained high volume, while on-demand per-token pricing wins for spiky low-volume traffic.
options: Choose provisioned throughput for sustained volume and on-demand for spiky use
Choose on-demand reservations for steady traffic and provisioned for trials
Choose fine-tuning jobs for latency control and evaluation for capacity
Choose Knowledge Base storage tiers to lock inference capacity pricing
q: A workload has sustained high-volume inference plus a separate spiky low-volume experiment. How should the team split Bedrock pricing?

explain: ROUGE-L measures summarization overlap automatically, while human review judges coherence and safety. BLEU targets translation and Guardrails enforce policy rather than score.
options: Score summaries with BLEU translation metrics and provisioned latency alone
Score summaries with ROUGE metrics plus structured human review of quality
Rank summaries using Guardrails block rates as the main accuracy metric
Compare summaries by token count and Knowledge Base chunk overlap only
q: A team must evaluate Bedrock-generated meeting summaries rigorously before production. Which metric combination is appropriate?

explain: Hybrid search combines semantic embeddings with keyword matching, and metadata filters restrict retrieval to the right tenant or document subset for accuracy.
options: Embed all tenants in one index and return the longest matching document
Raise the temperature so retrieval ignores tenant boundaries and finds more
Use hybrid search with metadata filters to scope retrieval per tenant topic
Disable chunking and pass every tenant document in a single giant prompt
q: A multi-tenant Knowledge Base returns irrelevant or cross-tenant passages. How should the team improve retrieval precision?

explain: Function calling with defined schemas lets the model request specific operations with validated arguments, unlike free-text replies that require fragile parsing.
options: Ask the model to describe the action in prose and parse verbs with regex
Let the agent guess endpoint URLs from training memory without schemas
Return all database rows to the model and let it pick the operation
Define function schemas so the model requests actions with typed arguments
q: A Bedrock Agent must reliably trigger order, refund, and shipping operations with correct arguments. Which design is most robust?

explain: Continued pre-training on domain corpora teaches terminology, then instruction fine-tuning shapes task behavior. A few generic prompts cannot instill deep domain knowledge.
options: Continue pre-training on domain corpora, then instruction-tune for tasks
Instruction-tune only on generic chats, then hope medical terms emerge
Replace training with longer prompts containing the full medical corpus
Run model evaluation jobs repeatedly until domain vocabulary appears
q: A medical startup needs a model fluent in clinical terminology that also follows task instructions. Which training sequence fits?

explain: Transcribe custom vocabularies fix domain terms during speech recognition, while call redaction masks PII in transcripts. Comprehend analyzes text after transcription instead.
options: Use Comprehend custom entities to decode trading-floor audio waveforms
Use Transcribe custom vocabulary plus PII redaction for trading-call audio
Use Polly lexicons to transcribe shouted orders into timestamped text
Use Textract AnalyzeDocument to transcribe speech with trader slang
q: Trading-floor recordings contain heavy slang plus sensitive card numbers that must not appear in transcripts. What should the team use?

explain: New items lack interaction history, so popularity or content-based fallbacks cover the cold start until behavior accrues. Waiting for retraining alone delays recommendations.
options: Exclude new listings from recommendations until a full yearly retraining
Force random new-item placement and ignore all interaction history signals
Blend popularity and content-based fallbacks until interactions accrue
Switch the campaign to a Forecast predictor trained only on new items
q: A marketplace adds hundreds of new listings daily with no interaction history. How should Personalize handle these cold-start items?

explain: Cold-start products borrow signal from related time series in the same group, plus item metadata, instead of relying on nonexistent history or fabricating rows.
options: Copy another product history verbatim and present it as the new forecast
Invent synthetic future sales rows to lengthen the new product history
Wait two years for history to accumulate before forecasting new items
Group new products with related series and add metadata for cold start
q: Forecast must predict demand for brand-new products with almost no sales history. Which cold-start strategy is sound?

explain: The robust pattern is retrieval-grounded Agents with tool actions, Guardrails filtering final output, and evaluation before launch. A bare model call lacks grounding, actions, and safety.
options: Call InvokeModel with long prompts and rely on users to verify policy text
Combine Knowledge Bases, Agents with actions, Guardrails, and evaluation
Fine-tune nightly on tickets and expose the endpoint without any filters
Route all questions to Lex slots and skip grounding and safety checks
q: A bank needs a support assistant grounded in policies, able to act on accounts, with safety filters and tested quality. Which architecture fits?
